```{r}
file_str <- "rosalind_revc.txt"
DNA_str <- readr::read_file(file_str)
```

```{r}
library(stringr)
```
You can't do this in a single string-replace because the function doesn't seem to
parse letter by letter, instead parsing the string repeatedly for each pattern (so T to A turns both the original Ts to A and the transformed Ts to A.) So, there's two options.
Neither of the ones I can think of are particularly elegant, but they will work.

Option 1:
```{r}
test  <- DNA_str |> str_replace_all(c("A" = "J", "T" = "A", "G" = "K", "C" = "G"))
test2 <- test |> str_replace_all(c("J" = "T", "K" = "C"))
test3 <- rev(str_split(test2, "")[[1]])
```

```{r}
revcomp_str <- paste(test3, collapse = "")
```

```{r}
cat(revcomp_str, file = "output.txt")
```
